tasks.name: Potty Shots
tasks.description: Forward Hike.  FORM: body in a squat, hands behind plate. Throw the plate forward using a two handed bowling ball rolling-like technique. The follow through should be low. Do not come out of the throw moving upwards. Follow throughs utilizing a monkey or a slight bulldog movement are allowed, flops are not.

tasks.name: Push Ups (10) + Run
tasks.description: Upper plank position, bring chest to the floor, moving entire body with it, Full ROM, core tight, head up, body flat.

tasks.name: Croakin
tasks.description: Hop forward using both legs landing in a squat and touching the turf with hands.  Continuously hopping and touching the turf.

tasks.name: Bear Crawl
tasks.description: Crawling forward on all fours.  FORM: make sure an even trade of arms and legs in an alternating manner (no galloping), using upper body just as much as lower.

tasks.name: Curl Walk 6+
tasks.description: Walking While Curling the plate.  At least 6 reps.  FORM: keep core tight, body straight (no leaning back), curl the plate up to face, elbows in, full ROM, plate turned down, use arms(not momentum).

tasks.name: Mogul Push
tasks.description: Plate Push, hoping feet together and side to side.

tasks.name: Plate Shake 9+
tasks.description: Holding the plate in front of chest, press the plate out (3/4 of a full extention), continuously. At least 9 reps.  FORM: never rest the plate on body (stop if rest is needed), don't tilt the plate, keep core tight, body straight (not leaning back), press the plate straight out in front (not up).

tasks.name: Monkey Crawl
tasks.description: Sideways crawl, alternating hands and feet. Start in the squat/crouch position, place hands to your side in the direction you are intending to move, placing all of your body weight on you hands/arms perform a cart-wheel-like crawl sideways. FORM:  keep body square to one side (no mongooses). Always face the same direction, similar to a shuffle, to that way your lead foot/hand changes.

tasks.name: Rev Bear Crawl
tasks.description: Crawling backwards on all fours. Each limb should move independently. Do not gallop, skate or wobble with your limbs.

tasks.name: Squat Thrust (10) + Run
tasks.description: Squat straight down bringing hands to the turf, then kick both feet back landing into a high plank position and immediately returning feet from which they came, last stand up so body is completely erect.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.
